'''''Delphinium elatum''''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the buttercup [[family (botany)|family]] [[Ranunculaceae]], known by the common names '''alpine delphinium''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007|accessdate=2014-10-17}}</ref> '''bee larkspur''', or '''candle larkspur'''. It is native to [[temperate climate|temperate]] Asia and Europe, it is an erect [[herbaceous]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] growing to {{cvt|1.8|m|ft|abbr=on}}, with deeply divided leaves. It produces spikes of blue or purple flowers in summer.<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/5398/delphinium-elatum/details | title = ''Delphinium elatum'' | publisher = RHS | access-date = 7 September 2021}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
''Delphinium elatum'' was one of the many species described by [[Carl Linnaeus]] in his 1753 work ''[[Species Plantarum]]''.<ref>{{cite book | author=Linnaeus C | title=Species Plantarum| volume=1| publisher=Laurentii Salvii |location=Stockholm | year=1753|chapter= Tomus I | chapter-url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/358550| page=531 |language=la}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
It is [[hardiness (plants)|hardy]] down to {{cvt|-20|C|F|abbr=on}}, but requires a sheltered position in full sun, and deep, rich soil. All plants must be securely staked to avoid the flower heads collapsing. Gloves should be worn when handling the plant, as it can cause severe discomfort if accidentally ingested.<ref name = RHSPF/>

''Delphinium elatum'' is a source of many ornamental [[cultivar]]s in a range of colours from blue and purple to pink, cream, and white.<ref name=sunset/>

[[Cultivar]] series include Magic Fountains,<ref name=rhs/> Pacific giant,<ref name=mbg/> Dwarf Pacific, New Millennium,<ref name=newmill/> and Aurora (six varieties: Blue, Deep Purple, Lavender, Light Blue, Light Purple and White).<ref name=gg/>

The following cultivars have received the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]]:
*'Lord Butler'<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/97251/Delphinium-Lord-Butler/Details | title = ''Delphinium elatum'' 'Lord Butler' | publisher = RHS | accessdate = 5 May 2020}}</ref> 
*'Sungleam'<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/98923/Delphinium-Sungleam/Details | title = ''Delphinium'' 'Sungleam' | publisher = RHS | accessdate = 5 May 2020}}</ref> 
*'Sweethearts' (New Millennium Series)<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/256285/Delphinium-elatum-Sweethearts-(New-Millennium-Series)/Details | title = ''Delphinium elatum'' 'Sweethearts' (New Millennium Series) | publisher = RHS | accessdate = 5 May 2020}}</ref>

==Chemical==
Seven C19-norditerpenoid alkaloids can be isolated from ''Delphinium elatum'': N-formyl-4, 19-secopacinine, iminoisodelpheline, iminodelpheline, iminopaciline, 6-dehydroeladine, elpacidine, and melpheline.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Chiba|first1=R|last2=Kanazawa|first2=R|last3=Matsuoka|first3=K|last4=Nakata|first4=A|last5=Tosho|first5=Y|last6=Asakawa|first6=E|last7=Suzuki|first7=M|last8=Ikuta|first8=M|last9=Yamashita|first9=H|last10=Wada|first10=K|title=Seven C19-norditerpenoid alkaloids from Delphinium elatum|journal=Planta Medica|date=Jul 2014|volume=80|issue=10|page=800|doi=10.1055/s-0034-1382523}}<!--|accessdate=26 April 2015--></ref>
